decisive_positive_evidence.explanation: A PM-chaired governing body was established to implement the Delta Plan 2100, showing concrete institutional control rather than slogan-only ambition.
The Power Division's ERP rollout and award show real administrative implementation across subordinate bodies.
The IMF staff-level agreement shows the authorities moving into a live macro-stabilization program under Hasina's government.
World Bank data on falling extreme poverty and improved services supports meaningful though lagged outcome progress.

decisive_negative_evidence.explanation: The IMF also notes unresolved vulnerabilities and the need for further investment, which caps claims of strong overall competence.
The same IMF agreement was crisis response after reserve stress, so it is not clean evidence of prior policy success.
The gains are retrospective and long-run, so they are only partially attributable to 2022 decision-making.

evaluations.inherited_baseline_and_constraints: Bangladesh entered 2022 with strong growth momentum but macro stress, reserve pressure, and pandemic aftereffects. I credited Hasina for real implementation capacity while treating long-run development gains, external demand, and crisis response as shared causes rather than personal mastery.
evaluations.ruler_attribution: Substantial but not exclusive. The record shows government-level implementation under Hasina with PM-chaired machinery and visible delivery, but many gains are institutional or retrospective rather than personally micromanaged.

contrary_evidence.explanation: Macro vulnerabilities and the need for more investment weaken any claim of exceptional performance.
Outcome gains are real but lagged and not uniquely 2022-owned.

evaluations.source_mix: Official government, IMF, World Bank, UNICEF, and contemporaneous media. The dossier is strong on formal implementation and outcomes, but several positive items are self-descriptions that I discounted unless independently echoed.
evaluations.structured_prior_summary: The priors point to middling-to-weak governance quality on accountability and rule of law, with relatively weak WGI government effectiveness and regulatory quality. I treated those as background constraints, not as score inputs.

material_biases.bias: Official and retrospective development sources can overstate continuity and understate bottlenecks.
material_biases.interpretation_effect: I credited real implementation but kept the score below the high anchor because several gains are institutional or retrospective rather than independently audited in-year.

material_biases.bias: The dossier is richer on macro and program architecture than on project-level delivery audits.
material_biases.interpretation_effect: This widens the plausible range because some competence is demonstrated by structure and follow-through, but not all outcome claims can be cleanly attributed.

bias_assessment.confidence_and_range_effect: Confidence is moderate-high because the record includes direct institutional action plus outcome data, but the score range remains wider than a pure legal-text case because attribution is partly indirect and several achievements are retrospective.
bias_assessment.remaining_uncertainty: The biggest uncertainty is how much of the development and macro performance is due to Hasina's 2022 choices versus inherited growth, external demand, and earlier reforms.

evaluations.chapter_rationale: Hasina scores moderately high on competence because the dossier shows a real governing program that was converted into institutions, operating mechanisms, and observable results. The Delta Plan was backed by a PM-chaired council; procurement, power-sector digitalization, education response, and macro stabilization all show more than symbolic direction. The strongest favorable evidence is not just rhetoric but implementation and some outcome improvement, including poverty reduction and faster, more transparent procurement. The limiting facts are that several achievements are institutional or retrospective, macro stress remained serious, and some claims are better read as state-level or ministry-level execution than personal micromanagement. I therefore place this above a merely mixed score but below a genuinely high score. Moral approval of the program did not affect the assessment.
evaluations.lower_anchor_rejected: A lower score would ignore the tangible implementation record: the PM-chaired Delta governance machinery, concrete ERP and policy execution, and measurable development gains are too substantial for a merely average or weak competence judgment.
evaluations.higher_anchor_rejected: A higher score is not warranted because key gains are partly inherited, indirect, or retrospective, and the dossier still records macro vulnerability and incomplete causal attribution for several of the best outcomes.

chapter_specific.value: Moral approval or disapproval of the government did not affect the competence score.
steady improvement with some macro stress and incomplete outcome attribution
Direct ruler micromanagement and independently audited project-level outcomes are thinner than the institutional record.

decisive_positive_evidence.explanation: Bolsonaro exerted direct pressure on Petrobras, showing real personal leverage over a core state asset.
His government actually ousted the Petrobras chief and altered fuel-price policy, which is concrete though politicized execution.
The election-year package shows the state machine was used for tactical mobilization, not just rhetoric.

decisive_negative_evidence.explanation: The fact-check compilation of repeated distortions undermines claims of disciplined or reliable program execution.
The campaign plan is a promise document, not proof of delivery, so it cannot carry the score upward much.
The TSE investigation shows institutional scrutiny of Bolsonaro's conduct in office and during the campaign.

evaluations.inherited_baseline_and_constraints: Brazil had institutional checks and a competitive electoral environment, but Bolsonaro's 2022 record was shaped by tactical power retention, budget stress, and a lot of performative rather than programmatic action. I credited the real use of executive power without confusing that with broad governing effectiveness.
evaluations.ruler_attribution: Direct for personnel pressure and election-year mobilization, but the record is weak on durable program execution and strong on tactical, contested, or self-serving choices.

contrary_evidence.explanation: The record is thick on false or distorted statements, which is bad for effectiveness because it weakens planning credibility and coordination.
The campaign platform is real program articulation, but it remains largely unexecuted in the dossier.

evaluations.source_mix: Mostly Reuters, official election/judicial records, and campaign material. The dossier is good for tactical moves and official pressure, but much weaker for durable, audited policy execution.
evaluations.structured_prior_summary: The priors are not especially weak institutionally, which makes the low score more about Bolsonaro's 2022 performance than about Brazilian state capacity as such.

material_biases.bias: Fact-check compilations and election-year press coverage overweight visible rhetoric and tactical conflict.
material_biases.interpretation_effect: I did not treat the volume of criticism as severity by itself, but the pattern still lowered confidence in the coherence of Bolsonaro's governing program.

material_biases.bias: The dossier has more evidence of tactical pressure than of durable program delivery.
material_biases.interpretation_effect: This keeps the score in the low-middle band rather than a true collapse score, because he still used state power effectively for some short-term objectives.

bias_assessment.confidence_and_range_effect: Confidence is fairly high because the evidence is direct and time-locked, but the score stays low because the record is mostly tactical power use rather than durable administration.
bias_assessment.remaining_uncertainty: The main uncertainty is how much to credit politicized state use as competence rather than as an indicator of narrow, self-protective control.

evaluations.chapter_rationale: Bolsonaro scores low on effectiveness because the dossier shows a president who could still use office power, but mostly for tactical pressure, coalition maneuvering, and election-year mobilization rather than durable governing competence. He pressed Petrobras, used the state machine around the campaign, and maintained some executive leverage. But the core record is dominated by repeated distortions, institutional scrutiny, and a policy portfolio that is more proclaimed than executed. The 2022 material does not show broad, sustained conversion of his stated program into effective state action. Moral judgment is not what drives the score; the issue is that his most visible choices did not translate into coherent, durable administrative progress.
evaluations.lower_anchor_rejected: A lower score would ignore the fact that Bolsonaro did achieve some concrete tactical control over personnel and policy levers, especially around Petrobras and the election-year state response.
evaluations.higher_anchor_rejected: A higher score is not justified because the dossier lacks durable, independently verified program execution and instead shows a pattern of rhetorical inflation, contestation, and tactical rather than administrative use of power.

chapter_specific.value: Moral disapproval of the rhetoric or campaign tactics did not itself determine the score.
short-term tactical gains, weak durable administration
Very thin durable-outcome evidence and weak support for broad policy execution.

decisive_positive_evidence.explanation: Xi secured a precedent-breaking third term and stacked the leadership with loyalists, showing strong elite control and strategic continuity.
The congress formally centered Xi and adopted his report and program, indicating effective conversion of authority into party-state action.
The central policy package was translated into implementation instructions to keep the economy stable.
Special inspections in 12 provinces and corrective follow-up show administrative enforcement rather than mere announcement.
R&D spending and intensity rose, consistent with sustained industrial and innovation priorities under Xi's system.

decisive_negative_evidence.explanation: The late-year COVID policy reversal after protests shows the system could adapt, but also that the earlier posture had become costly and reactive.
Property-sector rescue was corrective rather than preventive, which caps the score below the highest anchor.
Higher R&D inputs do not by themselves prove efficient conversion into output or broad productivity gains.

evaluations.inherited_baseline_and_constraints: Xi inherited a powerful party-state with major control capacity, and in 2022 he used it effectively to consolidate elite loyalty, push policy packages, and correct course when necessary. I discounted inherited centralization as such and asked whether his own program advanced; the evidence says yes, substantially, though not flawlessly.
evaluations.ruler_attribution: Strong. The major leadership reshuffle, program framing, economic dispatch, and policy correction all sit squarely within Xi's authority, even when implementation occurred through the State Council and regulators.

contrary_evidence.explanation: The zero-COVID reversal was a real correction but also a sign of policy strain and resistance.
The property rescue shows the state reacting to a serious problem rather than preventing it cleanly.

evaluations.source_mix: Official congress records, government notices, Reuters reporting, specialist analysis, and statistics. The dossier is heavily system-level but still includes clear ruler-linked choices and corrections.
evaluations.structured_prior_summary: The priors are consistent with a high-capacity authoritarian state: weak accountability, moderate rule of law, and strong government effectiveness. Those priors support a high ceiling but do not by themselves determine the score.

material_biases.bias: Official party-state sources can overstate coherence and understate implementation problems.
material_biases.interpretation_effect: I accepted the program and elite-control evidence but kept the score below the highest anchor because the dossier still shows reactive correction and sectoral stress.

material_biases.bias: Analytical reporting on elite control can over-read loyalty as competence.
material_biases.interpretation_effect: I treated loyalist stacking as competence only insofar as it advanced Xi's stated program, not as proof of broader economic or social success.

bias_assessment.confidence_and_range_effect: Confidence is high because the record is direct on leadership control and policy dispatch, but the score range remains open because outcome conversion is not equally strong across all priorities.
bias_assessment.remaining_uncertainty: The biggest open question is how much durable economic or social progress actually followed from the high-control political settlement, especially once the property and COVID strains are accounted for.

evaluations.chapter_rationale: Xi scores strongly because the dossier shows a ruler who turned political dominance into concrete governing machinery. He rewrote the elite team, re-centered the congress around his authority, pushed implementation notices, and used inspections and corrections to keep the system moving. The evidence also shows real policy follow-through on economic stabilization, industrial priorities, and late-year pandemic reversal. This is more than symbolic control: it is a full chain from program to enforcement to partial correction. I do not give a higher score because some major outcomes were reactive rather than preventive, and several favorable figures are inputs or policy moves rather than independently verified durable gains. Moral approval of the program did not matter here.
evaluations.lower_anchor_rejected: A lower score would miss the degree of elite control, administrative dispatch, and adaptive correction actually visible in the 2022 record.
evaluations.higher_anchor_rejected: A higher score is blocked by the fact that important successes are mixed with reactive crisis management and by the absence of equally strong evidence of durable outcome conversion across all major priorities.

chapter_specific.value: The score reflects program execution only; the political character of the program did not change the competence judgment.
strong consolidation with reactive correction under pressure
Outcome conversion is less clean than elite control and administrative direction.

decisive_positive_evidence.explanation: Tshisekedi personally chaired a major development-program evaluation meeting, indicating real executive attention and oversight.
The IMF said macroeconomic conditions improved and prudence increased, which is an actual policy-performance signal.
The EITI validation records tangible reforms with presidency-driven impetus, showing some implementation capacity.
The appointment and lack of inquiry around the Buhene episode show direct exercise of authority, even if the episode is a negative one.

decisive_negative_evidence.explanation: Corruption allegations around close associates show weak network discipline and only partial presidential response.
The mining audit found severe irregularities in a state asset, which tempers claims of clean governance.
The World Bank notes poverty reduction remained elusive, so growth did not translate cleanly into broad welfare progress.

evaluations.inherited_baseline_and_constraints: The DRC is a low-capacity, conflict-affected state with major inherited constraints. I gave Tshisekedi credit for some real oversight and policy activity, but I did not confuse inherited chaos or partner-led programs with full ruler competence.
evaluations.ruler_attribution: Mixed. The president clearly owns some oversight and appointment decisions, but the dossier repeatedly shows partial implementation, weak accountability, and substantial dependence on inherited structures and external conditions.

contrary_evidence.explanation: A damning audit of Gecamines shows major irregularities in a state company under presidential oversight.
The corruption allegations around close associates weaken any claim of disciplined control.

evaluations.source_mix: Official presidency pages, IMF, World Bank, EITI, OCCRP, HRW, and media. The mix is adequate but still tilted toward institutional and partner assessments rather than clean internal audits.
evaluations.structured_prior_summary: The priors are very weak on government effectiveness and regulatory quality, with only middling accountability and rule of law. That makes any real implementation noteworthy, but it also caps the plausible ceiling.

material_biases.bias: Official development and validation sources can overstate success in low-capacity settings.
material_biases.interpretation_effect: I kept the score at mixed rather than high because the positive evidence is real but not cleanly audited end to end.

material_biases.bias: The dossier is more visible on failures and corruption allegations than on quiet administrative competence.
material_biases.interpretation_effect: This raises uncertainty around the exact middle score without changing the basic judgment that the case is mixed.

bias_assessment.confidence_and_range_effect: Confidence is moderate because the record shows both real oversight and serious implementation failures, but several links in the causal chain remain incomplete.
bias_assessment.remaining_uncertainty: The main uncertainty is whether the positive institutional steps were durable enough to count as broad competence rather than episodic control.

evaluations.chapter_rationale: Tshisekedi lands in the middle because the dossier shows some genuine governing activity but not enough durable, ruler-attributed progress to justify a high score. He chaired a major development review, had some macro stabilization and EITI-backed reforms, and made meaningful appointments. But the same dossier shows mining irregularities, corruption allegations around close associates, and only partial implementation of broader welfare gains. This is not a collapse, but neither is it a strong delivery story. The evidence supports a mixed competence judgment rather than a materially higher one. Moral judgments about corruption or insecurity were not used as a separate penalty.
evaluations.lower_anchor_rejected: A lower score would ignore real presidential oversight, reform validation, and some macro improvement that are plainly present in the record.
evaluations.higher_anchor_rejected: A higher score is not warranted because delivery remains partial, corruption control is incomplete, and the welfare side of the program remains thin.

chapter_specific.value: The score reflects effectiveness, not approval of the program or the corruption allegations.
some institutional advance, but weak durable translation into broad outcomes
Direct household/outcome audit and personal attribution remain thin.

decisive_positive_evidence.explanation: Scholz personally set the wartime strategic direction and defense posture in his February 2022 statement.
The Bundestag approved the special fund, showing a real budgetary conversion of the post-invasion program.
The F-35 procurement was signed in 2022, moving the defense program from declaration to contract.
The cabinet enacted energy price brakes, a concrete crisis response rather than just rhetoric.
Concerted Action shows coordination with labor, business, and monetary actors to manage inflation.
Gas consumption dropped and import replacement occurred, indicating broader adaptation to the energy shock.

decisive_negative_evidence.explanation: The special fund had not yet reached troops in 2022, so delivery lag remained substantial.
The OECD notes real wages fell sharply and that better targeting was still possible.
Consumer relief was delayed into 2023, limiting the immediate outcome claim for 2022.

evaluations.inherited_baseline_and_constraints: Germany began from a high-capacity baseline but faced an acute wartime energy and inflation shock. I credited Scholz for converting crisis direction into budget, procurement, and price policy while treating procurement lag and wage pressure as real limits on the score.
evaluations.ruler_attribution: Strong but shared. Scholz drove the strategic turn and cabinet coordination, yet procurement, labor-market resilience, and gas adjustment also depended on ministries, firms, and external shocks.

contrary_evidence.explanation: The defense fund had not translated into troop-level spending in 2022.
Real wages still fell, which limits the claim of fully successful crisis management.

evaluations.source_mix: Strong mix of primary government speeches, Bundestag/ministry decisions, official statistics, and OECD corroboration. This is a high-quality dossier for execution and outcome, though still lagged on some defense outputs.
evaluations.structured_prior_summary: The priors are very strong on accountability, rule of law, government effectiveness, and regulatory quality. That supports a higher ceiling, but I still required visible 2022 execution rather than rewarding baseline capacity alone.

material_biases.bias: High-capacity democracies can look better because their paperwork and audit trails are stronger.
material_biases.interpretation_effect: I kept the score below the very top because documentation quality is not the same as immediate delivery.

material_biases.bias: Retrospective macro and labor data can over-credit the Chancellor for outcomes shaped by the war and prior capacity.
material_biases.interpretation_effect: This widens the range slightly and keeps the score in the strong-but-not-exceptional band.

bias_assessment.confidence_and_range_effect: Confidence is high because the dossier includes direct policy decisions plus official outcome data, but procurement lag and outcome timing prevent a tighter upper bound.
bias_assessment.remaining_uncertainty: The remaining uncertainty is how much of the favorable macro adjustment owes to Scholz versus inherited capacity and the specific shock environment.

evaluations.chapter_rationale: Scholz scores above the middle because he turned a severe external shock into a coherent program: rearmament, energy relief, inflation coordination, and budget conversion. The record is not just a speech record. The special fund passed, procurement advanced, price brakes were enacted, and Germany adjusted to the energy shock with measurable changes in consumption and imports. I do not go higher because the defense fund still lagged on delivery, real wages fell, and several of the best outcomes are only partly attributable to the Chancellor rather than to the whole German state. This is effective crisis governance, but not flawless execution. Moral approval of the security turn was not part of the score.
evaluations.lower_anchor_rejected: A lower score would undercount the clear conversion from post-invasion strategy into parliamentary, procurement, and energy-policy action.
evaluations.higher_anchor_rejected: A higher score is blocked by major implementation lag and by the fact that some of the best visible outcomes were not yet fully realized in 2022.

chapter_specific.value: The war-related security turn was judged only on execution, not on whether one approves it.
rapid crisis-driven implementation with lagged delivery
Defense procurement lag and short-run wage pain remain material constraints.

decisive_positive_evidence.explanation: The IMF program description shows a structured macro reform agenda with exchange-rate, fiscal, and structural pillars.
The FY2022/23 budget allocated large social-protection resources, showing a concrete policy choice under Sisi's government.
Sisi approved the State Ownership Policy Document, giving a clear formal step toward private-sector rebalancing.
The Saudi stake purchases show the asset-sale program moved from announcement into execution.
The World Bank monitor records policy response to FX stress and social mitigation measures, indicating active crisis management.

decisive_negative_evidence.explanation: The military-economy analysis highlights entrenched distortion and opacity, limiting how much competence can be credited to the presidency.
External shocks materially constrained choices, so some of the response is defensive rather than a clean success story.
The budget is a plan and target statement, not proof of realized household outcomes in 2022.

evaluations.inherited_baseline_and_constraints: Egypt's starting point was a stressed, state-heavy economy with FX pressure and heavy military involvement. I credited Sisi for real policy architecture and some execution while treating the structural distortions and external shocks as serious constraints on the upper score.
evaluations.ruler_attribution: Moderate. The presidential approvals and policy framework are real, but a lot of the record is state- and ministry-level implementation under heavy inherited constraints rather than a clean personal execution record.

contrary_evidence.explanation: State-heavy military economics and opacity weaken any claim of strong, clean implementation competence.
Budget allocations do not prove realized welfare outcomes.

evaluations.source_mix: IMF, World Bank, official ministries, and market reporting. The mix is adequate, but much of the positive record is formal policy architecture and program launch rather than audited delivery.
evaluations.structured_prior_summary: The priors are middling on accountability and rule of law, with weakish governance effectiveness and regulatory quality. That matches a state that can still execute selected reforms but not with high efficiency.

material_biases.bias: Official reform announcements may overstate actual implementation in a state with opaque military-linked sectors.
material_biases.interpretation_effect: I kept the score at six rather than pushing higher because program architecture is clearer than independently audited delivery.

material_biases.bias: Macro stress can make crisis management look weaker than it would under calmer conditions.
material_biases.interpretation_effect: This widens uncertainty but does not change the basic mixed-competence judgment.

bias_assessment.confidence_and_range_effect: Confidence is moderate-high because there are real policy steps and some executed transactions, but the outcome side is still thin.
bias_assessment.remaining_uncertainty: The main uncertainty is how much of the apparent progress reflects durable reform versus a narrow, state-led adjustment to a forced FX crisis.

evaluations.chapter_rationale: Sisi scores in the upper-middle range because the dossier shows a government that could still generate formal policy architecture and some execution under severe pressure. The state-ownership document was approved, social protection was funded, the asset-sale program moved forward, and the IMF and World Bank records show real crisis-management activity. But much of this is defensive and state-heavy rather than a clean record of broad competence, and the military-economy background limits how much credit can be given for efficiency or execution quality. The evidence supports a solid but not standout score. I did not lower the score because the program is illiberal; competence is the only question here.
evaluations.lower_anchor_rejected: A lower score would ignore the clear policy architecture, presidential approvals, and some actual asset-sale execution visible in the dossier.
evaluations.higher_anchor_rejected: A higher score is blocked by structural opacity, heavy inherited distortion, and the lack of independently audited household-level outcomes.

chapter_specific.value: The score reflects execution and adaptation only, not the political system's morality.
structured but defensive reform under stress
Household-level welfare outcomes and private-sector rebalancing remain thin.

decisive_positive_evidence.explanation: The IMF visit records a clear structural-reform agenda for the Abiy administration.
The national anti-corruption committee announcement shows active top-level oversight and enforcement intent.
The auditor-general appointment shows staffing choices that support the reform agenda.
The audit office's recovery and system-wide audit work shows some real enforcement and institutional follow-through.
State-enterprise profit and revenue gains show at least some strong state-sector performance under the umbrella of the administration.

decisive_negative_evidence.explanation: Aid access delays during the Tigray truce show implementation friction under severe constraints.
The IMF notes remaining delays in SOE reporting, limiting claims of clean reform execution.
Recovery of funds and prosecutions do not prove broad, non-selective anti-corruption success.

evaluations.inherited_baseline_and_constraints: Ethiopia in 2022 was constrained by war, fragmented authority, and severe state stress. I gave Abiy credit for reform architecture and some oversight capacity, but the evidence does not support a high score because the dossier is still thin on independent delivery and clean causation.
evaluations.ruler_attribution: Moderate. The reform agenda and committee appointments are attributable to Abiy's administration, but the hardest outcomes are still shaped by war, donor support, and unresolved implementation bottlenecks.

contrary_evidence.explanation: Access delays after the truce indicate serious implementation friction.
The IMF still observed reporting delays and incomplete institutional maturation.

evaluations.source_mix: IMF, official Ethiopian reporting, Reuters, and local reporting. The mix is decent, but some of the best material is self-reporting and still leaves war attribution unresolved.
evaluations.structured_prior_summary: The priors are weak-to-middling on governance effectiveness and regulatory quality, with only moderate rule-of-law signals. That fits a state capable of selective reform but not clean, broad execution.

material_biases.bias: Government-aligned sources can overstate reform momentum in a conflict-stressed state.
material_biases.interpretation_effect: I credited the reform agenda but kept the score from rising into a strong band because independent delivery proof is limited.

material_biases.bias: Conflict and implementation delays can obscure real but partial institutional gains.
material_biases.interpretation_effect: This increases the uncertainty band rather than changing the overall mixed judgment.

bias_assessment.confidence_and_range_effect: Confidence is moderate because the dossier shows real reform activity, but the causal chain is still broken by war, delay, and incomplete audit evidence.
bias_assessment.remaining_uncertainty: The biggest uncertainty is how much of the reform record is durable Abiy-driven capacity versus donor-assisted or short-lived administrative adjustment.

evaluations.chapter_rationale: Abiy lands slightly above the middle because there is genuine evidence of reform architecture, anti-corruption coordination, and some institutional follow-through. The government set a structural-reform agenda, created a national anti-corruption committee, appointed an auditor-general, and produced some measurable audit and SOE signals. But the dossier is still burdened by war, access delays, and incomplete independent verification of outcomes. That makes the competence story real but partial. I would not score it much higher because the most favorable items are still mixed with implementation problems and unresolved attribution. Moral evaluation of the war context was not part of the score.
evaluations.lower_anchor_rejected: A lower score would ignore the real reform agenda, staffing decisions, and audit follow-through that do appear in the 2022 record.
evaluations.higher_anchor_rejected: A higher score is not justified because independent delivery evidence is thin and major implementation frictions remain visible throughout the dossier.

chapter_specific.value: The score reflects execution capacity and adaptation, not approval of the conflict environment.
reform intent with partial institutional follow-through under severe stress

decisive_positive_evidence.explanation: Jokowi set the 2022 budget priorities, showing a clear governing program tied to social and infrastructure goals.
He chose and justified ministers on competence grounds, indicating deliberate personnel selection.
He pushed downstream mining policy and cited a concrete success, showing policy follow-through.
Nusantara development had started with concrete infrastructure milestones, which is real implementation.
The emergency regulation replacing the jobs law is a direct executive act that shows adaptation and speed.
The IMF records solid GDP and deficit outcomes for 2022, despite external noise.
Inflation was managed at a difficult moment through coordinated policy choices.

decisive_negative_evidence.explanation: Deputy-minister expansion for coalition management shows power politics as well as administration, which is a mixed sign for competence.
The emergency-regulation route was controversial and contested, so it is not a pure success marker.
The IMF explicitly credits favorable external conditions too, so not all macro success is Jokowi-owned.

evaluations.inherited_baseline_and_constraints: Indonesia entered 2022 with reasonably strong state capacity, but also with inflation pressure, coalition management demands, and a huge flagship capital-city project. I credited Jokowi for concrete execution and adaptation while keeping causal credit partial where the dossier itself flags external drivers.
evaluations.ruler_attribution: Strong for budget-setting, appointments, and policy direction; moderate for macro and outcome claims because commodity prices, the post-pandemic rebound, and external demand matter too.

contrary_evidence.explanation: Some personnel choices were coalition-management tactics rather than clean meritocracy.
Macro gains were partly driven by external conditions.

evaluations.source_mix: Official presidential statements, World Bank, IMF, Reuters, and Bank Indonesia. The dossier is strong on direct policy direction and outcome data, with some attribution caveats on the macro side.
evaluations.structured_prior_summary: The priors show fairly strong governance and decent government effectiveness. That is consistent with the dossier's concrete rollout evidence and helps explain why Jokowi lands in the upper band.

material_biases.bias: Official announcements and presidential speeches may overstate readiness, especially on flagship projects.
material_biases.interpretation_effect: I rewarded real implementation, but not as if the entire program were already complete.

material_biases.bias: Strong macro outcomes can over-credit the president for results partly driven by commodity prices and post-pandemic rebound.
material_biases.interpretation_effect: This keeps the score high but not exceptional because the causal split is not fully ruler-owned.

bias_assessment.confidence_and_range_effect: Confidence is high because there is repeated direct evidence of implementation and some independent outcome corroboration, but the range remains slightly wider because causality is partly shared.
bias_assessment.remaining_uncertainty: The biggest uncertainty is the true durability and completion rate of the flagship projects, especially Nusantara, versus the more immediate budget and macro actions.

evaluations.chapter_rationale: Jokowi scores high because the dossier shows consistent conversion of a program into action: budget priorities, personnel choices, downstream industrial policy, infrastructure start-up, labor-law adaptation, and macro management. The evidence is not just rhetoric; there are concrete decisions and measurable 2022 outcomes, including growth and inflation control. I still stop short of a very high score because some positive outcomes are partly inherited or externally driven, and some of the best projects are still at rollout stage rather than audited completion. This is strong operational competence, especially by the standards of a diverse cabinet and a large economy. Moral judgments about specific policy choices were not part of the score.
evaluations.lower_anchor_rejected: A lower score would understate the volume of concrete implementation and the repeated pattern of policy conversion visible in the dossier.
evaluations.higher_anchor_rejected: A higher score is blocked by external causation in the macro data and by the fact that several flagship initiatives were still midstream.

chapter_specific.value: The score reflects program execution, not endorsement of any policy direction.
broad policy conversion with concrete rollout and some macro success
Project completion and causal attribution for the strongest outcomes remain incomplete.

The program had operationalized planning bodies and data layers, showing machinery rather than rhetoric.
Project-monitoring data and review suggest substantial implementation coverage and bottleneck management.
The PMG portal shows many issues were being resolved, which is concrete administrative follow-through.
The later review confirms the scale of the GIS and project-examination system.
The recruitment task force shows a direct implementation response to a PM-directed staffing target.

decisive_negative_evidence.explanation: Inflation remained above the tolerance band for a prolonged period, limiting the claim of clean macro success.
Hundreds of projects still had time overruns and bottlenecks, so the rollout was incomplete.

evaluations.inherited_baseline_and_constraints: India began 2022 with substantial state capacity but severe inflation and administrative complexity across a federal system. I credited Modi for strong program rollout and monitoring while keeping causal credit below perfection because many outcomes were still shaped by external shocks and uneven subnational execution.
evaluations.ruler_attribution: Strong. The program design, monitoring architecture, and staffing directives are plainly Modi's; the main caveat is that execution is shared with ministries, states, regulators, and the RBI.

contrary_evidence.explanation: Inflation pressure remained acute, so the macro side was not cleanly solved.
Execution bottlenecks and time overruns mean the infrastructure story is not fully complete.

evaluations.source_mix: Strong mix of prime-ministerial speeches, PIB releases, World Bank, RBI, Reuters, and project-monitoring data. The evidence base is rich on rollout and monitoring, but some outputs are still measured through government self-reporting.

evaluations.chapter_rationale: Erdoğan scores slightly above the middle because the dossier shows a ruler who still wields real authority and converts it into diplomacy, macro intervention, and some measurable outcomes. He mediated a grain corridor, helped broker a prisoner exchange, pushed economic measures, and oversaw a large investment program. However, the macro environment is badly distorted by inflation, and several visible successes are only partial or externally conditioned. That means the score is decent but not exceptional. The chapter is about effectiveness, so the fact that he operates in an illiberal system does not itself help or hurt the score.
evaluations.lower_anchor_rejected: A lower score would miss the real diplomatic influence and policy conversion documented in the dossier.

evaluations.chapter_rationale: Biden scores high because the record shows real policy conversion: legislation, executive action, implementation guidance, grant deployment, and early outcome signals. This is not a case of paper programs alone. The Infrastructure Law and IRA were turned into administrative machinery, the DPA was used to push industrial production, and the OECD sees a strong rebound backed by policy. I do not go higher because independent audits still find process weaknesses, and the macro story is partly shared with shocks and other institutions. Still, this is a strong governing performance. The moral character of the policy goals did not affect the score.
evaluations.lower_anchor_rejected: A lower score would ignore the combination of legislation, executive implementation, and early outcome signals that make the 2022 record materially strong.
evaluations.higher_anchor_rejected: A higher score is blocked by audit findings, implementation friction, and the fact that macro outcomes are not all uniquely Biden-owned.

evaluations.chapter_rationale: Trọng scores well because the dossier shows disciplined agenda-setting, serious anti-corruption enforcement, useful macro outcomes, and active foreign-policy execution. He is not just issuing slogans: the anti-corruption campaign has concrete personnel turnover, the national plan has target language, and the external-facing diplomacy is real. I keep the score below a very high band because some of the biggest programs, especially the recovery package, still show slow disbursement and incomplete translation from plan to delivery. This is a competent party-state performance, but not flawless mastery. The score is about execution, not moral judgment of the regime.

batch_notes: Anchors used across the batch: Bolsonaro and Putin at the low edge, Tshisekedi/Buhari/Prayut/Sharif/AMLO in the middle-low band, Hasina/Scholz/Erdoğan/Kishida/Trọng/Marcos in the upper-middle band, and Xi/Modi/Jokowi/Biden as the high end.
I scored on ruler-attributed conversion of program into action and progress, not on moral approval, regime type, or source volume alone.
Official self-report, retrospective outcome claims, and advocacy material were discounted when not independently supported; independent audit, multilateral, and legal records carried more weight.
Missing lenses widened confidence ranges rather than mechanically lowering scores, and no blank democracy/autocracy correction was applied.
